# incident-tool-routing-v1

**Fully synthetic and fictional.** No real logs, systems, companies or people. Generated by
[toolroute-06b](https://github.com/Pranjulcr7/toolroute-06b) v0.1.0 (`toolroute generate --seed 0`) on top of the
simulator in [agent-reliability-lab](https://github.com/Pranjulcr7/agent-reliability-lab).

Each row asks for the **single next step** given a request, eight tool schemas (in the system message) and prior
tool results: a tool call with arguments, a clarifying question, a refusal, or a direct response.

| split | rows | sha256 |
|---|---|---|
| train | 1,991 | `860743a8fe05…` |
| validation | 300 | `b6c2b4b84cbc…` |
| test | 300 | `113aca55d077…` |

**Fields:** `messages` (system + user, ready for a chat template), `completion` (gold JSON string), `target` (parsed),
`kind`, `template_id`, `world_id`, `structure`, `step`, `heldout_structure`, `history`, `authorized_proposals`.

**Generation method:** request templates × fictional worlds. Tool results were produced by actually executing calls
on the simulator. Labels come from deterministic oracle code, not from a model. Every gold call was schema-validated
and executed against a replay of its history. No paid or teacher-model generation was used.

**Leakage controls:** splits are disjoint in request templates, entity names, worlds/trajectories and prompts. The test
split contains 64 examples from incident structures absent from training.

**Known gaps:** single-step requests are nearly keyword-solvable (a regex router scores 0.97–1.0 on them);
English only; one author wrote both the templates and the baseline; 3 remediation actions; 1 runbook; 9 incident
structures; response/clarification texts are templated.

**Version:** 1.0.0 (2026-09-26). License: Apache-2.0.
